title: Joseph the Worker (1 May)
hookLine: the carpenter of Nazareth, kept on the first of May, the day set aside for workers

lines: A SHOP IN A SMALL TOWN.
cards: A workbench. Shavings curled on the floor. A plane, a saw, a few nails in a dish.
On the first of May, a day when marchers in cities carry banners for workers, the Catholic calendar sets this bench in the middle of the church. Not a throne. Not a battlefield.
A shop in a small town, and a man whose hands smelled of wood. Today, Joseph the Worker.

teach.h: THE TOWN SAYS: THE CARPENTER'S SON.
teach.b: The Gospels say almost nothing about Joseph's job. It comes up once, and not as praise. Jesus is teaching in his home town, and the neighbors can't get past where he comes from.
In the Douay-Rheims: "Is not this the carpenter's son?" The Greek word behind carpenter, tektōn, can mean someone who works in wood, or more widely a builder or craftsman.
Either way, the town is saying: we know this family. They work with their hands, like us. Here's the turn.
The feast takes that sneer and makes it the whole point.

teach.h: JESUS GREW UP IN A WORKING HOUSE.
teach.b: The Son of God, as they believe him to be, grew up in a working house and learned a trade beside Joseph. For the years the Gospels skip, tradition pictures him simply at work.

teach.h: ORDINARY LABOR IS NOT TIME AWAY.
teach.b: So the feast makes a quiet claim: ordinary labor is not time away from God. Sanding a door, stocking a shelf, answering the same email again.

The Church gave Joseph a feast on the workers' day so that the day would have a saint in it. Catholics keep this feast in more than one way. Some pray for their own work, asking Joseph to help them do it honestly.
Others keep it for people who can't find work at all, or who work in danger, or for too little.

teach.h: NO WORD OF JOSEPH'S IS RECORDED.
teach.b: And some notice that the Gospels never record a single word spoken by Joseph.

teach.h: IS NOT THIS THE CARPENTER'S SON?
teach.b: He is remembered for what he did, not what he said.

how: On 1 May the Catholic calendar keeps an optional memorial of Saint Joseph the Worker; Catholics often pray for workers and the unemployed, and some parishes bless tools or hold Masses for labor.

games.q: you're choosing a feast day for the patron of workers. the first of May already belongs to the workers' marches. what do you do?
o: pick a quiet day nobody else uses.
set Joseph's feast on that very day.
skip it: work isn't a church matter.
games.why: the Church set Joseph the Worker on the first of May, so the workers' day would have a saint in it, a carpenter.

practice: Bring to mind, one at a time, people looking for work: someone sending applications into silence, someone whose job ended with an injury, a closing or a cut, someone ashamed to say so.
If you pray, ask Saint Joseph to stand beside them at the next door they knock on; if you don't, simply hold them in mind, and the dignity of what their hands can do.

wordCard.voice: Tekton, the Greek word for carpenter, or craftsman. Joseph the Worker, kept on the first of May, is honored for silent work Catholics treat as holy.
